stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

---
name: continual-arc
description: Solve Continual-ARC grid instances; emit exactly one valid action JSON per turn and infer transformations from demos.
---

# Continual-ARC

1. Treat each puzzle instance as a strict action protocol: the entire reply must be exactly one JSON object (`submit` with a grid, `request_demos`, or `finish`), with no preceding or trailing explanation, Markdown, or other text. Do not call shell or other tools to send an action; the JSON reply itself is the action.
2. Read attempt and demo budgets. Request demos only when their expected information is worth the cost; account for demo-request costs as well as wrong submissions. Before guessing, compare all supplied input-output pairs cell by cell, record the exact changed cells and unchanged candidate objects, and test a rule against every pair. Do not act on an analogy or a partial alignment until it explains every observed change and non-change. If the rule remains ambiguous and budget permits, request another demo.
3. Derive output dimensions and layout from the demonstrations. Infer the full output rule, including both the condition for changed cells and the value of every other cell; do not assume a detected overlap or match is the output background. Verify the complete rule cell by cell against every demo before applying it, then check row count, each row length, cell range (0–9), and JSON validity before submitting.
4. After feedback, revise the hypothesis only from the correctness result or a new demo. A correct/incorrect result does not identify which cells were wrong; do not treat speculative explanations as evidence. Submit only when the rule is sufficiently supported; use `finish` only after the instance is over.

[5,1,5,5,1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1],

O=np.zeros((11,12),bool); O[1,1]=1;O[2,8]=1;O[3,2]=1;O[6,0]=1;O[8,5]=1
print('O coordinates match L?',[(r,c,L[r,c],R[r,c]) for r,c in zip(*np.where(O))])
for flip in [False,True]:
 for shift in range(-11,12):
  # relate output x to source x+shift or reflected
  pred=np.zeros_like(L)
  for r in range(11):
   for c in range(12):

    if 0<=j<12: pred[r,c]=R[r,j]
  if np.array_equal(pred,O): print('exact map R',flip,shift)
  if np.array_equal(pred,L & ~O): print('LminusO',flip,shift)
print('overlaps L/R',np.argwhere(L&R).tolist())
print('union L/R',np.argwhere(L|R).tolist())
